lines: Q: What's the hardest part of meals for you? Or something else.
A: Deciding what to make every day, with everyone's different rules. That's the hardest part.

Q: Which apps do you order groceries on: Zepto, Blinkit, Instamart, BigBasket or Amazon? If you sign me in, I'll read your past orders to learn what your home buys and how often, so the plan and the shopping list fit you from the first week, and I can fill the cart for you. Nothing is ordered without your yes.
A: We don't use any apps, the kirana delivers.
Q: I have Ankit (34), Pooja (32), Reyansh (8), Ramesh (66) and Kamla (62) eating at home. Anyone else who eats at home, or anyone who doesn't?
A: That's everyone, no one else. All five of us.
Q: Who cooks at home, and on which days? Is any day's meal eaten out?
A: Pooja cooks every meal, every day. We never eat out.
Q: What did the children have for breakfast over the past week? Tell me in as much detail as you can.
A: Reyansh had poha, paratha, besan chilla, or dalia — whatever we make for everyone. He's the only child.
Q: The children's lunch over the past week, or their school tiffin?
A: Reyansh takes tiffin to school Mon-Fri: paratha with sabzi, poha, aloo sandwich.
Q: The children's dinner over the past week?
A: Same as everyone — roti and a sabzi, gatte ki sabzi or aloo matar or bhindi. Khichdi on Saturday night.
Q: What did the adults have for breakfast over the past week? Tell me in as much detail as you can.
A: Same as Reyansh — poha, paratha, besan chilla, dalia. Papa has dalia sometimes.
Q: The adults' lunch over the past week?
A: Dal, chawal, roti, ek sabzi. Kadhi chawal sometimes. Dal baati on Sundays.
Q: The adults' dinner over the past week?
A: Same as I said for Reyansh — roti and a sabzi, gatte ki sabzi or aloo matar or bhindi. Khichdi on Saturday night.
Q: Is anyone on a diet? High protein, low carb, diabetic, anything a doctor asked for.
A: No, nobody's on any diet. We all eat the same.
Q: Do the elders eat anything differently from the rest: less salt, softer food, no onion or garlic, a fasting day?
A: Papa never eats onion or garlic. Mummy doesn't eat them on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
Q: Any food rules for the house? Veg, egg or non-veg days, fasting days, allergies, a dish someone won't touch.
A: Pure vegetarian, no eggs in the house. Papa never eats onion or garlic, Mummy skips them on Tuesdays and Thursdays. No one has allergies or fasting days.
A: sorry I meant Mummy's no onion garlic days are Tuesday and Saturday, not Thursday
Q: How often do you order in, and on which days?
A: We don't order in at all. Pooja cooks every meal.
Q: Does anything come on a subscription, like Country Delight or a milkman?
A: We get milk from the local dairy, 2 litres daily. No subscriptions.
